'''Moisés Hassan Morales''' (born 4 May 1942)<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|last=Affairs|first=United States Department of State Bureau of Public|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8o04esLcobwC|title=Nicaraguan Biographies: A Resource Book|date=1988|publisher=U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Public Affairs|pages=26–28|language=en|access-date=2020-12-17|archive-date=2021-01-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131231014/https://books.google.com/books/about/Nicaraguan_Biographies.html?id=8o04esLcobwC|url-status=live}}{{PD-notice}}</ref> is a Nicaraguan politician. He was one of five members of the [[Junta of National Reconstruction]] that ruled the country from 1979 to 1984, following the fall of the [[Somoza family|Somoza]] regime.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last1=DeYoung |first1=Karen |title=Uneasy Alliance of Rebels, Businessmen to Rule Nicaragua |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1979/07/22/uneasy-alliance-of-rebels-businessmen-to-rule-nicaragua/b4dafb1c-0bfe-4440-a98a-f37fb8c905fc/?tid=a_classic-iphone&no_nav=true |access-date=16 December 2020 |newspaper=Washington Post |date=22 July 1979 |archive-date=31 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131231028/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1979/07/22/uneasy-alliance-of-rebels-businessmen-to-rule-nicaragua/b4dafb1c-0bfe-4440-a98a-f37fb8c905fc/?tid=a_classic-iphone&no_nav=true |url-status=live }}</ref>

== Early life ==
Born in [[Managua]] on May 4, 1942, to a Nicaraguan mother and Palestinian father from [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] (then part of [[Mandatory Palestine]]),<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /> Hassan studied engineering at the [[National Autonomous University of Nicaragua]] (UNAN).<ref name="NYT">{{Cite news|date=1979-07-18|title=Sketches of the Nicaraguan Junta's Five Members|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1979/07/18/archives/sketches-of-the-nicaraguan-juntas-five-members-sergio-ramirez.html|access-date=2020-12-16|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=2021-01-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131231015/https://www.nytimes.com/1979/07/18/archives/sketches-of-the-nicaraguan-juntas-five-members-sergio-ramirez.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1968, he earned a PhD in physics from [[North Carolina State University]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Inventory of the Moisés Hassan M. papers|url=https://oac.cdlib.org/findaid/ark:/13030/kt9c6036gq/entire_text/|access-date=2020-12-17|website=oac.cdlib.org|archive-date=2020-08-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200805202329/https://oac.cdlib.org/findaid/ark:/13030/kt9c6036gq/entire_text/|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Career and militancy ==
Hassan was a long-time dissident and early FSLN member. He attended his first protest against the Somoza dictatorship in 1958 and was jailed several times for his continued dissidence.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news|last=Kinzer|first=Stephen|last2=|first2=|date=1988-05-08|title=In Managua, Not Exactly Last Hurrah (Published 1988)|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/05/08/world/in-managua-not-exactly-last-hurrah.html|url-status=live|access-date=2020-12-29|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=2016-07-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160728151152/http://www.nytimes.com/1988/05/08/world/in-managua-not-exactly-last-hurrah.html}}</ref> He joined the FSLN in its infancy in the 1960s and was a key figure in the organization by the time the uprising came to a head in the late '70s, having built a network of subversives in Managua’s slums.<ref name=":3" /> 

He was the dean of the UNAN's College of Science and Letters until he joined the anti-Somozas effort in 1978.<ref name=":0" /> He was head of the activist [[National Association of Professors]] and became its delegate to the [[United People's Movement (Nicaragua)|United People's Movement]], a coalition of civic groups supporting the Sandinistas, which he founded in 1978.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" />

He led the September 1978 uprising against the regime.<ref name=":3" />

In 1979, he joined the five-member [[Junta of National Reconstruction]] (RN), alongside fellow Sandinistas, intellectual [[Sergio Ramírez]] and commander [[Daniel Ortega]], as well as [[Violeta Chamorro]], widow of [[La Prensa (Managua)|''La Prensa'']] publisher [[Pedro Joaquín Chamorro Cardenal]]; and prominent businessman [[Alfonso Robelo]]. Hassan left the RN in March 1981.<ref name=":1" /> 

Hassan served as Minister of Construction until he became Vice-Minister of the Interior in May 1983.<ref name=":1" /> From 1984 to 1988, he was [[Mayor of Managua]].<ref name=":2" /> His technical skills made him valuable in that capacity, dealing with persistent flooding in the capital.<ref name=":3" />  

Hassan split with the FSLN in 1988.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Ameringer|first=Charles D.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kD5qi3MyEHYC|title=Political Parties of the Americas, 1980s to 1990s: Canada, Latin America, and the West Indies|date=1992|publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group|isbn=978-0-313-27418-3|pages=473|language=en|access-date=2020-12-16|archive-date=2020-10-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201003133413/https://books.google.com/books/about/Political_Parties_of_the_Americas_1980s.html?id=kD5qi3MyEHYC|url-status=live}}</ref> He was removed from his post as Mayor for failure to follow orders from the nine-member FSLN National Directorate, at times at odds with ideological hardline members [[Tomás Borge]] and [[Bayardo Arce]].<ref name=":3" /> Hassan resigned the party shortly thereafter.<ref name=":3" />

On December 16, 2009, he published ''La maldición de Güegüense.''<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mendieta Herdocia|first=Mauricio|date=2009-12-24|title=Comentarios al libro de Moisés Hassan "La maldición del Güegüense"|url=https://www.laprensa.com.ni/2009/12/24/opinion/11261-comentarios-al-libro-de-moises-hassan-la-maldicion-del-gueguense|access-date=2020-12-18|website=La Prensa|language=es|archive-date=2021-01-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210131231046/https://www.laprensa.com.ni/2009/12/24/opinion/11261-comentarios-al-libro-de-moises-hassan-la-maldicion-del-gueguense|url-status=live}}</ref>

His papers are held at the [[Hoover Institution Library and Archives]] at [[Stanford University]], acquired in 2002.<ref name=":2" />
